African megafauna.note: Africa keeps the intact big-mammal community - elephants, rhinos, hippos - that other continents lost.

Burgess Shale biota.note: The 508-Ma community of British Columbia - the fullest window on Cambrian soft-bodied animals anywhere.

Cambay amber flora (Dipterocarpaceae).note: Fifty-million-year-old amber from Gujarat holds a dipterocarp rainforest, and insects with Asian relatives: India was already trading life across a narrowing sea.

Cathaysian flora.note: The tropical coal-forest flora - Gigantopteris, Lobatannularia - that built the great Shanxi coals.

Cerrado flora.note: Fire-adapted savanna woodland with thick corky bark and vast root systems.

Cerrejon rainforest.note: The oldest neotropical rainforest known: palms, legumes and aroids in a structurally modern canopy only a few million years after the asteroid, and hot enough to support Titanoboa.

Chengjiang Biota.note: An early Cambrian Lagerstatte in Yunnan, older than the Burgess Shale and just as detailed -- soft tissue, guts and nervous systems.

Chinchilla fauna.note: The Chinchilla Local Fauna of the Darling Downs, Queensland -- a Pliocene assemblage recording Australia's rainforest-to-woodland shift, misfiled by name-collision with the South American rodent.

Dachstein reef fauna.note: The Late Triassic reef community of the Tethyan carbonate platforms -- scleractinian corals, calcareous sponges and encrusting problematica.

Doushantuo biota.note: Weng'an phosphorites preserving algae and controversial embryo-like fossils at cellular resolution, ~600 Ma.

Dwyka glacial fauna.note: Cold marine faunas in the seas around a Gondwana buried under Carboniferous ice.

East Kirkton tetrapods.note: A Scottish Mississippian hot-spring site preserving early terrestrial tetrapods such as Westlothiana.

Ediacaran biota.note: A grab-bag of frondose, discoid and quilted organisms whose relationships to living animals are still argued about a century after their discovery.

Emu Bay Shale biota.note: A South Australian Lagerstatte where Anomalocaris keeps its compound eyes - tens of thousands of lenses each.

Endemic trilobites.note: Isolated on its own tropical craton, Siberia grows a distinctive Ordovician trilobite fauna.

Fezouata biota.note: Moroccan mudstones extend Burgess-type soft-bodied preservation into the Ordovician of the Saharan shelf.

Glossopteris flora.note: The whole cool-temperate seed-fern forest - Vertebraria roots, Gangamopteris - that defines Permian Gondwana.

Gotland reef fauna.note: Silurian Gotland is a fossilised barrier reef of tabulate and rugose corals and stromatoporoids.

Hirnantia fauna.note: A cold-water brachiopod assemblage that spread worldwide as end-Ordovician ice gripped the Saharan pole.

Jehol Biota.note: The Yixian and Jiufotang beds of Liaoning: volcanic ash falls that buried a whole forest ecosystem intact, feathers, stomach contents, colour-bearing melanosomes and all.

Karoo therapsids.note: The Karoo Basin of South Africa preserves the mammal-like reptiles in unbroken sequence across the end-Permian extinction -- the best record anywhere of that catastrophe on land.

Luoping biota.note: A Middle Triassic marine Lagerstatte in Yunnan documenting the recovery of ocean life after the extinction.

Malvinokaffric fauna.note: The Bokkeveld Group and Parana Basin preserve the cold-water Devonian brachiopod-trilobite province.

Malvinokaffric flora.note: Early sparse vegetation of horsetails and progymnosperms on the southern floodplains.

Mbuji-Mayi microbiota.note: The Tonian Mbuji-Mayi Supergroup yields acritarchs and vase-shaped microfossils - genuine eukaryote fossils from the craton's cover.

Meishan fauna.note: The Meishan section is the global boundary marker for the end-Permian extinction, in continuous marine limestone.

Messel biota.note: An Eocene oil-shale lake in Germany preserving bats, early horses and gut contents in mirror detail.

Morrison fauna.note: The Late Jurassic Morrison Formation - Allosaurus, Stegosaurus, Apatosaurus, Diplodocus - the archetypal dinosaur bonebed.

Orsten fauna.note: Alum-shale nodules of Sweden preserve millimetre crustaceans in uncrushed three-dimensional phosphate.

Orthoceratite fauna.note: The red 'Orthoceras limestone' of Sweden and Estonia is a graveyard of straight-shelled cephalopods.

Permian tetrapods.note: Amphibians and early reptiles of the Permian rivers, the northern counterparts of the Karoo fauna.

Rhynie chert biota.note: A Scottish hot-spring deposit that silicified an entire Early Devonian land ecosystem where it stood.

Sahni's nests.note: Titanosaur nesting grounds across the Deccan, eggs laid on the flood basalt itself between eruptions.

Siberian Traps flora.note: The last forests before the Great Dying, buried under the largest volcanic eruption of the eon -- the coal seams of Tunguska are their remains.

Sinsk biota.note: An Early Cambrian soft-bodied Lagerstatte in anoxic Siberian shelf muds, older than the Burgess Shale.

Small shelly fauna.note: The Siberian Platform yields the type Tommotian assemblage - the first mineralised skeletons, mostly millimetre tubes and spines.

Tendaguru fauna.note: The Late Jurassic Tanzanian beds preserve Giraffatitan and Kentrosaurus - Africa's answer to the Morrison.

Tingamarra fauna.note: The lone substantial early-Cenozoic Queensland site (~55 Ma), hinting at South American mammal links, then near silence.

Trilobite biomeres.note: The shallow sea records repeated sudden trilobite mass-extinctions and rebounds - the classic 'biomere' pattern.

Trilobite provinces.note: Trilobites so different on its two shores that the contrast first revealed the ocean's former existence.

Yanliao Biota.note: The Daohugou beds: Middle-Late Jurassic lake deposits with salamanders, feathered dinosaurs and the earliest gliding mammals.

cryoconite communities.note: The best candidate refugium for photosynthetic life through the Sturtian and Marinoan glaciations.
